sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Justice Dr. V.R.K.Krupa Sagar
 Criminal Petition No.5505 of 2024
Order:

1. This Criminal Petition, under Sections 480 and 483 of the BNSS is filed seeking to enlarge the petitioner/accused on regular bail in connection with Crime No.38 of 2024 of Varadhaiahpalem Police Station of Tirupathi District for the offences punishable under sections 302, 436, 498A, 435 of the IPC.

entities.text: Varadhaiahpalem Police Station of Tirupathi District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. Heard arguments of Sri P.Madhu Sudhan, the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent/ State.
3.
On hearing the learned counsel on both sides and on perusal of the record, it is seen that the deceased is a lady and the petitioner/accused is her husband.
The allegations are that the petitioner was suspecting the fidelity of his wife.
It is stated that the married couple were blessed with two children.
The victim lady was in the house of her parents.
The accused used to come to in-law's house and used to stay there and used to go back.

On 19.04.2024, he was in the company of his wife and the wife went to take a bath and from the bathroom, the family members heard the cries of the victim lady and when they reached the spot, they found the accused outside the bathroom.
The victim lady was found unconscious with blood oozing from the mouth lying on the floor of the bathroom.

She was immediately taken to a doctor where first aid was given, and the victim lady gained consciousness and told her father that the accused was abusing her about her chastity and forcibly hit on her cheek and as a result, she fell down and the accused pressed her throat.
It is further alleged that accused came to the hospital and once again quarreled with his wife and removed her thali from her neck.
The victim lady was shifted to bigger hospital where while undergoing treatment, she succumbed to injuries and died on 20.04.2024.
It is further alleged that the accused even burnt a beeruva.
4. In Crl.M.P.No.547 of 2024, the accused sought bail and by an order dated 26.07.2024, the learned VI Additional District and Sessions Judge, Chittor dismissed the same.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Chittor
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned APP opposed the prayer for grant of regular bail.
5. It is seen that the petitioner was arrested on 24.04.2024 and was remanded to judicial custody.
Thus, for the last more than four and half months, he has been in judicial custody.
It is stated by both sides, that the investigation is over.
There are no criminal antecedents against the petitioner.
Case facts depict emotional causes resulted in commission of the alleged acts.
According to learned counsel for petitioner, he is the sole bread winner of the family and has to maintain the children.
6. Considering the length of detention and the near completion of investigation, this court finds that any continued detention does not seem necessary.
Hence, prayer is granted.

sentences.text:
In the result, this criminal petition is allowed in the following terms:
The petitioner/accused shall be enlarged on bail on executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand only) with two sureties of the like sum each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Junior Civil Judge, Puttur,
FAC/ Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, Sathyavedu, Tirupathi District.
The petitioner shall mark his attendance before the Investigating Officer on 1st and 15th of every month between 10.00 AM and 1.00 PM till filing of the charge sheet.

The petitioner shall make himself available for investigation by a police officer as and when required, and he shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any persons acquainted with the facts of the case to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
He shall not indulge in similar acts of crime.

Dr. V.R.K.KRUPA SAGAR, J Date: 10.09.2024 Dvs THE HON'BLE JUSTICE Dr. V.R.K.KRUPA SAGAR CRIMINAL PETITION No.5505 of 2024 Date:
